ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The table in the figure lists the rankings of the climate change vulnerability index of some countries. Among 171 countries, Bangladesh ranks 1st, India ranks 2nd, Madagascar ranks 3rd, Nepal ranks 4th, and Mozambique ranks 5th; the lower part of the table also lists Sweden, Ireland, Iceland, Finland, and Norway ranked 167th to 171st respectively. From this it can be seen that India's climate change vulnerability index ranking is very near the top. Then reason: The question requires judging India's most common extreme weather by combining the frequency with which India suffers extreme climates. India mainly belongs to a tropical monsoon climate, with relatively high temperatures throughout the year and obvious seasonal variation in precipitation; before the arrival of the rainy season and during the dry season, high-temperature and little-rain phenomena are prominent, and heat waves, droughts, and other dry-hot conditions easily occur. Therefore, the extreme weather with the highest frequency in India may be dry and hot weather.
